article.name: CIRIS Agent
article.summary: CIRIS Agent is an open-source assistant and agent framework whose memory is a typed graph exposed through a memory service and action bus. The checked-in Python service delegates persistent node and edge operations to the ciris-persist engine; nodes are keyed by identifier and scope. This is a source-based review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

who_what.text: CIRIS Agent is an open-source assistant and agent framework with a typed graph-memory service integrated through its memory bus and action pipeline. The official repository identifies the project organization as CIRISAI; this review does not infer individual maintainers from commit metadata.

architecture.text: Graph nodes carry an identifier, type, scope, attributes, version, updater, and update time. Attributes may include creator, content, timestamps, tags, and node-specific fields. Edges store endpoints, relationship, scope, optional weight, and context. The four scopes are LOCAL, IDENTITY, ENVIRONMENT, and COMMUNITY.

The Python persistence adapter routes graph operations through ciris-persist. It addresses a node by ID and scope, merges attributes on update, increments the optimistic version, and delegates scoped reads and deletes to the engine. The repository persistence documentation names SQLite and PostgreSQL backends.

behavior.text: MEMORIZE validates typed parameters and uses the memory bus. User-node writes check consent and managed attributes; identity changes require Wise Authority authorization and use an engine-managed amendment path. The memory service processes secret-bearing attributes before persistence.

An update reads the existing node, merges incoming attributes over the stored attributes, and passes the expected current version to the persistence engine. The reviewed adapter does not show an immutable prior-value history table. FORGET checks Wise Authority authorization for IDENTITY and ENVIRONMENT scope and requests a hard delete; the adapter says the engine cascades deletion to connected edges. Backup, synchronization, and external-copy retention were not established.

RECALL tries exact node-ID lookup in the requested scope first, then falls back to search. Search enumerates up to its requested limit (100 by default), then matches case-insensitive substrings against IDs and serialized attributes; the inspected path does not provide semantic ranking. Wildcard recall lists a bounded number of nodes by scope/type and optional graph traversal returns connected nodes.

All inspected reads are scope-aware, and selected writes/deletes carry Wise Authority checks. Scope describes graph memory categories; the checked memory-service API does not accept a principal identity as a query predicate. Per-user or tenant isolation for principals sharing one agent store was not established.

metrics.evidence: Exact ID lookup and bounded substring search are source-visible; no answerability or abstention probes were run.
The persistence adapter merges attributes and increments the node version; no correction sequence was scored.
The adapter requests hard node deletion with an edge cascade; no residual-copy or post-delete probes were run.
Queries are scope-filtered and some writes/deletes require Wise Authority checks; no multi-principal isolation workload was run.
Nodes and edges carry metadata and the project documents a decision audit trail; no evidence adjudication was run.
The source path was inspected but not timed.
The service exposes operation and database-size fields, but no resource measurements were collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded review of selected documentation and current source at the verified head. It does not establish runtime behavior, behavior of the external ciris-persist engine beyond the checked adapter contract, backup/sync retention, access-control behavior outside inspected action paths, or production isolation between principals.

The inspected text-search path matches substrings across a bounded set and shows no semantic ranking. Updates merge values and advance a version, but these files do not establish prior-value history. The separately documented decision audit trail is not evidence that every previous memory value is recoverable.
No system operation, benchmark workload, or tests were run. Project metric definitions and fixtures describe evaluation plans and are not CIRIS Agent results.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run. This review did not execute CIRIS Agent, its tests, or benchmark workloads.
